source_refs.note: Lymph Nodes and Lymphoid Masses: a main subheading of 11.5 Lymphatic system of human, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 255-255.

blocks.text: At certain spots, the lymph vessels have masses of connective tissue where lymphocytes are present. These are lymph nodes. Several afferent lymph vessels enter a lymph node and the lymph is drained by a single efferent lymph vessel. Lymph nodes are present in the neck region, axilla and groin areas of man. In addition to lymph nodes, several lymphoid masses are present in different areas e.g., in the mucosa and submucosa of alimentary canal. The larger lymphoid masses are spleen, thymus, tonsils and adenoids. These produce lymphocytes.

blocks.alt: A round lymph node with a green capsule enclosing compartments of lymphocytes and macrophages. Several lymph vessels (lymphatics) bring lymph in round the edge; one lymph vessel drains lymph out at the top, beside a blood vessel pair where blood enters and drains.
